destination.name: Rajshahi
destination.description: Rajshahi is the capital of Rajshahi Division in Bangladesh. The city is near many ancient capitals of Bengal, notably Lakhnoiti (or Lokhnaboti), and Pundra. Rajshahi is famous for trade in many exotic items, including pure silk, mangoes and lychees. Attractive silk products are cheaper in Rajshahi than anywhere else in the country, with the city often referred to as the 'silk city'. There are also a number ancient mosques, shrines and temples in and around Rajshahi.

places.name: T Bandh
places.description: A lovely sight of one of the largest rivers in South Asia. During the Monsoon season, the water level rises, along with its beauty.

places.name: Varendra Research Museum
places.description: Established in 1910, the museum is dedicated to ancient history and culture. It is recognised as the oldest museum in the country. It has a rich collection of artefacts, relating to Hindu, Buddhist and Muslim heritage. Some of these date back to the 16th century. It is maintained by the University, located in the heart of town.

places.description: The park is a wide area with lush green trees and grass. The zoo houses a variety of different animal species. It is by the bank of river Padma.

places.description: A historical mosque situated in Bagha, Rajshahi. There is a picture of this mosque in one side of the Tk 50 note.

places.name: Kismat Maria Mosque
places.description: An old mosque in Durgapur Upazila, a short distance from Rajshahi city. It was built around 1500 and is a protected archaeological site listed by the Department of Archaeology of Bangladesh.

places.name: Puthia Rajbari
places.description: The present two-storey rectangular palace was built in 1895 by Maharani Hemanta Kumari Devi in an attractive Indo-European style. The front pillars, ornamentation, woodwork, and floral and vine paintings on the room walls and above the doors show fine craftsmanship. The roof is flat and made of iron beams, wooden rafters, and tiles. A moat was dug around the palace for security. There are six…

places.name: Krishnapur Gobinda Mandir
places.description: A square temple, 4.25 m on each side, with doorways in the east and south walls. The arched east doorway is the main entrance, and it is decorated on both sides and above with terracotta plaques. The south doorway has little decoration. The temple has a tall shikhara (spire) roof topped with a finial, and its cornices and corners are finely decorated with terracotta plaques. The outer west wall…

places.name: Pancha Ratna Govinda Temple
places.description: Built in the 19th century. It has the architectural feature of five ratnas or spires.

places.name: Shaheb Bazaar
places.description: A raucous street scene of commerce.

places.name: RDA Market
places.description: On the south side of Shaheb Bazaar, this is the largest market in Rajshahi, full of vendors selling clothes, food, cosmetics, etc.

places.name: New Market
places.description: A bit more shopping mall-like, but another large market with both hawkers and higher-end vendors.

places.name: Kumarpara Mor
places.description: At this point you will find some renowned brand shops like Arong, Le reve, Richman etc.

places.name: Pancha Ratna Shiv Temple
places.description: It is the largest shiv temple in Bangladesh. The temple consists of five spires and hence the name. Each of the spires consists of several sub-spires. The corner spires each have 17 sub-spires, while the large central spire consists of 108 sub-spires. The temple was constructed by Rani Bhuban Mayi Devi, the widow of Raja Jagat Narayan Ray, jamindar of Puthia. The temple was completed in 1830.…

places.name: Rath Mandir
places.description: Like the nearby Pancha Ratna Shiv Temple this temple was also constructed by Bhuban Mayi Devi. The date of construction is 1823 (another opinion 18390). It is dedicated to Lord Jagannath. Although much shorter than its neighbouring temple the Rath Temple has its share of elegance. The octagonal two-storied temple is topped with a dome-like structure topped with a finial. The white-coloured temple…

places.name: Dol Mandir
places.description: Built in 1778 the four-storied structure stands on a square base. Each stories reduces proportionally. The first stage has 7 arches on each side, the second stage has 5 arches on each side and the third stage has three arches on each side. The topmost stage has a single arch on each side and is topped with a dome.

places.name: Pancharatna Gobinda Mandir
places.description: This is one of the most spectacular terracotta temples of Bangladesh. The temple is located within the Putia Rajbari Complex. The temple consists of five pinnacles (locally known as ratnas) and hence the name. The 18th-century temple was built by one of the queens of the Puthia zamindar family. The temple has a triple arch entrance complete with elaborate and intricate terracotta ornamentation.

places.name: Rani Hemanta Kumari Residence
places.description: This was the private residence of Hemanta Kumari Devi, the lady who built the Puthia Rajbari.

places.name: Rani Ghat
places.description: This is a private bathing ghat for the queen. It is located on Shiv Sagar and is an enclosed space used by women to bathe privately.

places.name: Choto Annik Mandir
places.description: This is a small temple following the do chala style of Bengal temple architecture. The front facade has a triple arch entrance with elaborate terracotta ornamentation.

places.name: Choto Shiv Mandir
places.description: This is a very small temple following the char chala style of architecture. The front facade has elaborate terracotta ornamentation.

places.name: Char Ani Palace
places.description: In 1744 the Puthia Zamindari was divided among the 4 brothers. The brothers were identified by the shares they received. One of these four brothers, who got a char ani share built this mansion. But, unlike the Puthia Rajbari (also known as panch ani) this is in utter ruins. The complex is approached through a gate. Large portions of the mansions including the roof has long collapsed. A few…

places.name: Gopal Temple
places.description: Just north of the char ani mansion and on the west bank of Shyam Sagar lies a small temple complex housing three temples. These are Gopal Temple, Choto Gobindo Temple and Boro Annik Mandir. The Gobindo Temple is located on the left of the entrance, It is a two-storied temple without any ornamentation.

places.name: Choto Gobindo Mandir
places.description: This is located next to the Gopal Mandir and as the name suggest follows the char chala style of Bengal temple architecture. The front faced has a triple-arched entrance complete with elaborate terracotta ornamentation.

places.name: Boro Annik Mandir
places.description: The east facing temple follows a mixed style of Bengal temple architecture. The central part follows the do chala style and is flanked on both sides by two char chala structures. The front faced of the do chala section has a triple-arched entrance. The two char chala sections have a single arched entrance. The front face of the temple has elaborate terracotta ornamentation.

restaurants.description: Offers indoor, outdoor, and rooftop seating with views of the Padma River. The venue serves a variety of local, continental, and fast food items, making it a favorite spot for evening hangouts and family dining.
